I am writing this review to warn others about my extremely frustrating and unacceptable experience with StealthEX. My funds have been locked on their platform for over 4 days now, with no sign of a resolution in sight. The core issue is simple: I accidentally sent BEP-20 (BSC) USDC to an ERC-20 address when creating an exchange. I immediately contacted support to rectify the error.

The problems began when StealthEX insisted that the only way to refund my funds was to provide a video recording of our company's internal payment system and wallet history. This is a demand we cannot comply with due to our own strict corporate security protocols, a point we have explained repeatedly. We offered a very simple and logical solution: to use the USDC-BSC tokens that they already hold (currently sitting in their wallet address 0x521839a39312bda5b483170dc5c5c6200b7be4ab) and complete the swap to USDC-ERC using a new exchange I created. This would resolve the issue and bypass their problematic video verification requirement.

Despite this clear and technically viable solution, StealthEX has refused to act, claiming it is "technically not possible to swap the same asset," even though this would be a cross-network swap from BEP-20 to ERC-20, which is a basic function for their platform. Their support has provided no clear technical reason for why this simple solution is impossible.

My experience has been met with a total lack of urgency or customer focus. Here is a summary of the failures:

Unreasonable Verification: Demanding a video of a corporate system is a major security breach that we, and likely many other businesses, cannot permit. No alternative verification methods are offered.

Lack of Logic & Technical Support: The support team completely ignored a clear, step-by-step solution that would have solved the problem in minutes, instead insisting on their impossible demands.

Horrendous Delays: What should have been a simple error correction has dragged on for over 4 days. Their support team constantly provides vague updates like "this will take some time" and, most recently, asked for an additional 24 hours just for an update—not even a resolution.

Misleading Process: It seems the platform can receive funds even when an exchange is technically impossible, but they are either unwilling or unable to reverse the transaction or complete the simple network swap.

StealthEX is holding a significant amount of our funds hostage over a bureaucratic and security-compromising process. I strongly advise anyone against using this platform, as a simple user error can lead to your assets being locked away for days with no logical path to recovery. It feels like a textbook case of holding customer funds hostage to force compliance with unreasonable demands.

Timestamp: This has been ongoing since June 26, 2026.

Update: It looks like the process has gotten back on track after about 7 hours since my transaction was accepted. I changed the rating accordingly (personally, I'd give 2.5 stars, but that's just me being picky).

--------------------------------------------------

It is entirely unacceptable for a financial institution to be unable to process a refund due to liquidity issues with a partner, especially when no estimated timeframe for resolution is provided. Such a lack of transparency and accountability is deeply troubling.

For context, I have extensive experience doing business with multiple financial firms (the UK's banking and its associates did make it more challenging to run a business that required stocking cryptocurrencies to maintain a minimum volume to offer reliable services). I am well aware that liquidity problems can occur and are not uncommon. However, in every previous case I have experienced, these institutions promptly rolled back, refunded, and upheld the basic expectations for working with or investing in cryptocurrencies. When a transaction is confirmed, the expectation is clear: the only step left is to wait for the coins to be released to the customer, so it would be understandable if a refund were complicated. 

Yet, when funds are held due to liquidity issues before a transaction is finalised, there is no legitimate reason not to refund. The refusal to do so, coupled with a failure to respond to follow-up inquiries, clearly indicates that my funds are being intentionally withheld. It is widely acknowledged that some institutions exploit such situations to profit during internal holding periods while charging substantial fees. This practice is already highly unethical, but given the crypto market's volatility and the hostility from large banks that resist coins they cannot control, I will accept it and move on.

It should go without saying to seasoned investors that:

A financial entity facing liquidity problems with its (crypto) currencies, withholding customers’ funds without a clear resolution timeline, and refusing to release or refund failed transactions fundamentally undermines trust in the company's internal state. Such behaviour is especially egregious within the UK’s strong regulatory environment, which already makes the industry reliant on cryptocurrency much more burdensome.

Moreover, it is well understood that even short delays -- such as five minutes -- can have serious financial consequences in high-risk markets like cryptocurrency, but this is inherent to how blockchains operate.
 However, having your funds held hostage is unreasonable and can cause severe financial damage to investors.

Once again, the indefinite delay and withholding of customers’ funds are utterly unacceptable. Endorsing StealthEX under these conditions would be tantamount to endorsing misconduct.

It is profoundly concerning that my only recourse to address these issues is through this public forum, as your support team has ignored my follow-up inquiries within the ticketing system. This pattern of silence and generic responses demonstrates a lack of regard for customer accountability and raises serious questions about the integrity of your operations.
